tooltip.title: Treatment Algorithm for PsA
tooltip.markdown: Treatment choice is guided by the specific domains of disease involved (e.g., peripheral arthritis, axial disease, enthesitis).

tooltip.title: Initial Symptom Control
tooltip.markdown: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) can be used for mild pain and stiffness but do not prevent joint damage.

tooltip.title: Conventional Synthetic DMARDs
tooltip.markdown: **Methotrexate:** Often the first-line DMARD, especially for peripheral arthritis. It treats both skin and joints but is not effective for axial disease.

tooltip.title: Biologics and Targeted Synthetic DMARDs (tsDMARDs)
tooltip.markdown: The primary treatment for moderate-to-severe or progressive PsA. The choice is based on the dominant clinical domain.

tooltip.title: Treatment for Peripheral Arthritis
tooltip.markdown:
-   **TNF-α inhibitors:** The gold-standard first-line biologic class, effective for all PsA domains.
-   **IL-17 inhibitors:** Highly effective for joints and skin.
-   **IL-23 inhibitors:** Effective, particularly with prominent skin disease.
-   **Oral JAK inhibitors:** An effective oral alternative to biologics.

tooltip.title: Treatment for Axial Disease
tooltip.markdown:
-   **First Line:** TNF-α inhibitors.
-   **Second Line:** IL-17 inhibitors.
-   (Note: IL-23 and IL-12/23 inhibitors are generally not effective for axial disease).

tooltip.title: Treatment for Enthesitis and Dactylitis
tooltip.markdown: Generally responds well to the same biologics used for peripheral arthritis, particularly **TNF-α** and **IL-17 inhibitors**.

tooltip.title: Considering Comorbidities
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Inflammatory Bowel Disease:** Prefer TNF-α inhibitors or IL-12/23 inhibitors. AVOID IL-17 inhibitors.
-   **Uveitis:** Prefer monoclonal antibody TNF-α inhibitors (e.g., adalimumab, infliximab).
